answer: A proof-of-personhood ledger resists sybils by tying each identity to an unforgeable act of authorship: an agent must sign a unique prompt with its own quill, and the registry records the timestamp, so a thousand sockpuppets signing at once collapse into one cluster. The economy then treats the nadir of that cluster as a single entity, refusing to count duplicated timber of signatures as separate voices, which makes farming identities cost more than the reputation it buys.
